title: Retention recommendation engine and autosuggest for route TTLs
creator: Nadia Kapoor
description:
Context:
Redwood customers need simple, safe defaults for how long prompt/response artifacts, request logs, and derived metrics are retained. Many customers are unsure how to pick TTL values across per-route, per-tenant, and global policy layers. Choices today are manual and error-prone, leading to either excessive storage costs or regulatory exposure.

Goal:
Deliver a retention recommendation engine and autosuggest UX in the Console that: (1) analyzes route usage, latency/cost profile, and customer residency constraints, (2) produces human-readable TTL suggestions (e.g., 30d/90d/365d or custom policy templates), and (3) can generate a signed attestation bundle (evidence export) showing reasoning for auditors. The feature should reduce time-to-configuration and lower accidental over-retention.

Scope:
- Ingest per-route telemetry (request volume, avg tokens, peak QPS), per-tenant residency setting, and configured SLAs.
- Run heuristics + ML-lite model to recommend TTL presets per artifact class (prompts, responses, request logs, metrics).
- Provide confidence indicators and cost delta estimate (monthly $) for suggested TTLs.
- Autosuggest UI: inline suggestion chip in Route Settings with 'Apply suggestion' and 'Preview export' actions.
- Generate an evidence bundle (JSON) that includes input signals, chosen heuristics, and an HMAC-signed statement for compliance teams.

Non-goals:
- Not implementing legal-hold enforcement in this ticket (separate legal-hold flow).
- Not replacing tenant-level policy authoring DSL; recommendations only produce suggested policies for approval.

Success metrics:
- 30% reduction in time-to-set-retention for new routes (measured in Console funnel events).
- 25% of suggestions accepted by customers within first 6 weeks of rollout.
- No false-suggested TTL that violates explicit tenant residency constraints (0 violations post rollout).

Technical approach:
1) Signals: lightweight aggregator job (ENG) will expose a per-route summary API (7d/30d histograms, token distribution, cost estimates).
2) Recommendation engine: rule-based core + small logistic model for confidence scoring. Rules prioritize residency, SLA, and cost.
3) Evidence bundler: compose a compact JSON with input signals, rule evaluation trace, and signature using platform KMS.
4) Console integration: show suggestion in UI with cost delta and 'Preview evidence' modal. 'Apply' emits an audit event and optionally triggers policy patch.

Acceptance criteria:
- Backend API returns suggestions for 95% of routes within 200ms for a single route query.
- Console displays suggestions and a working "Preview evidence" modal for selected routes.
- Evidence bundle includes deterministic trace of rule evaluations and a signature; sample bundles stored for QA.
- E2E tests cover telemetry ingestion -> suggestion -> apply patch flow.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- ML vs rules: starting with rules simplifies auditability. We may later surface ML-derived signals but must keep traceability for compliance.
- Signature format: HMAC vs KMS-signed JWT; HMAC is quicker to ship but KMS-signed JWT preferred for enterprise.
- Cost estimation accuracy: we will surface an estimate bucket (low/medium/high) until we can provide dollar-accurate forecasts.

Stakeholders:

- Engineering: ENG-51234 (telemetry/aggregator), ENG-33782 (retention infra), infra security
- Design: DES- (UX mocks to be attached)

Next steps / milestones:
- 2026-02-25: Telemetry summary API contract review (ENG-51234).
- 2026-03-05: Console mock and review (Design) -> feedback captured.
- 2026-03-12: PoC of rule engine + sample evidence bundle (this ticket: In Progress).
- 2026-03-26: Internal pilot with two customers and acceptance metrics collection.

Notes on uniqueness:
This work focuses on a recommendation-first UX and signed evidence bundles for auditors — unlike prior tickets which emphasize policy authoring or retention-simulator UIs. The emphasis here is on operationalizing safe defaults and attaching an auditable rationale to each suggestion.
